acceptance: For a query subset, the estimate is derived from the tables read, and a test covers a subset, the full benchmark, and an unknown query id (which falls back to the full estimate).
Measured peak memory for at least three subset runs per engine is recorded in this item and is below the estimate in every case.
The refusal message says whether the figure is a subset or full-benchmark estimate.
description:
Problem. The DataFrame memory guard estimates memory for the whole benchmark at a scale factor (`estimate_memory_required(benchmark, scale_factor, platform)` in `benchbox/core/dataframe/capabilities.py`), so a run of three TPC-DS queries at SF10 is refused with an 18-20 GiB requirement although those queries read a few tables and ran on a 16 GiB host in an earlier measurement. Users must pass `--ignore-memory-warnings`, which also removes protection for runs that really are too large.

Owner decision 2026-11-13: not built with the message fix, because an estimate that is too low could let a run exhaust a shared host. This item exists so the option is not lost.

Expected: when a query subset is selected, the estimate reflects the tables those queries read, with a stated margin, and never falls below a measured floor for the platform.

Guardrails: the guard must stay conservative; validate the estimate against measured peak memory on at least Polars, DataFusion and PySpark before it gates anything. Timings and memory measurements only through `make heavy-run`.
